findings.problem: BatchWorkflow has no typestate state machine; mark_sent mutates fields arbitrarily without enforcing valid transitions, allowing illegal state combinations (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with no corresponding lifecycle data).
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct or mutate BatchWorkflow into any combination of fields, making illegal states fully representable and undetectable at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace struct fields with a typestate enum (e.g. enum BatchStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }) and remove mark_sent mutator; transitions become constructor-only via enum variants.

findings.problem: status: String is a raw primitive for a lifecycle concept. Any string value is accepted (e.g. "foo", "SENT", "").
findings.failure_mode: Invalid status values silently pass; pattern matching on status becomes exhaustive-failure-prone if/else chains instead of compile-time guaranteed transitions.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum: pub enum BatchStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and use it in place of status: String.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that encode state as independent bits rather than enforced transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Four independent boolean-like states (validated+sent, validated+not_sent, not_validated+sent, not_validated+not_sent) include semantically invalid combinations that the type system cannot reject.
findings.fix: Collapse both booleans into a single typestate enum variant that owns the lifecycle data (see typestate_state_machine finding).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is optional lifecycle data stored outside the lifecycle state machine. It can be Some when status is not sent, or None when status is sent.
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some<u64> for a non-sent batch, or None for a sent batch, creating inconsistent lifecycle data that violates domain invariants.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }, making the data owned by the variant that needs it.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive domain identifier with no constraints, validation, or newtype protection.
findings.failure_mode: Any String (empty, whitespace, oversized, non-UTF8 surrogate) is accepted as a batch ID. No domain rules (length, format, uniqueness) are enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: pub struct BatchId(String); with a smart constructor that validates constraints, or use a domain-specific ID type from the start.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly. The struct is public with all pub fields and there is no parse layer.
findings.failure_mode: External callers bypass all domain invariants by directly constructing BatchWorkflow with invalid field combinations, because no smart constructor or parse function validates inputs before they reach the domain.
findings.fix: Make all fields private, remove the no-arg constructor, and provide a single parse function that accepts DTO primitives, validates them with fallible smart constructors, and returns a BatchWorkflow (or domain error). Replace all field types with domain types (enum, newtype, typestate) in the parsed result.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns BatchWorkflow with no typed error. There is no validation of preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent) and no error type for failure modes.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent silently accepts invalid preconditions (e.g. marking a non-validated batch as sent) with no feedback to the caller; errors are invisible.
findings.fix: Return Result<BatchWorkflow, BatchError> with a typed error enum (e.g. BatchError::NotValidated, BatchError::AlreadySent) and validate preconditions before mutating state.

findings.problem: All fields on BatchWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to bypass mark_sent and any future validation logic by directly mutating fields.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set item.status = "" or item.is_sent = true directly, completely bypassing the mark_sent function and any validation it might add.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (pub(crate) at minimum) and expose state through methods or derived views. Only the typestate enum variant should expose its data.

findings.problem: No canonical build or test commands have been executed. The crate does not even contain a test module, so cargo test cannot validate behavior.
findings.failure_mode: The code may not even compile under strict clippy gates (arithmetic_side_effects, as_conversions, etc.) and no behavior is verified.
findings.fix: Add at minimum: cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features, and cargo clippy with strict warnings. Add tests that exercise the domain invariants.

residual_risk: All findings are BLOCKER-level domain model violations. The struct makes every illegal state representable via public String/bool/Option fields with no typestate enforcement, no parse boundary, no error taxonomy, and no smart constructors. The code compiles as trivial Rust but violates every Holzman law regarding type-driven DDD, panic freedom, bounded invariants, and functional core architecture. Delivery is blocked until the struct is replaced with a typestate enum, parse boundary with fallible smart constructors, and typed error taxonomy.
